title: Risk of Virological Failure After Switch to a Tenofovir‐Sparing Dual Therapy in Virologically Suppressed People With HIV and Past HBV Infection

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study compared the effectiveness of tenofovir (TFV)-based triple regimens to TFV-sparing dual therapies in virologically suppressed people living with HIV who had past HBV infection (HBsAg−/HBcAb+).
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study emulated a target trial including 415 adults from five University Hospitals with HBsAg−/HBcAb+ serostatus who started a triple regimen with unsuppressed serum HIV-RNA and reached suppression. Participants were mainly men (329, 79.3%) with a median age of 48 years, and 71 (17.1%) started a dual therapy during follow-up.
analysis.methods: The probabilities of virological failure, defined as two consecutive HIV-RNA ≥ 50 cp/mL or a single HIV-RNA ≥ 200 cp/mL, were estimated through a weighted Kaplan–Meier estimator.
analysis.main_results: In the weighted analysis, the estimated probabilities of virological failure at 5 years were 29.3% for dual therapy and 29.9% for triple therapy (difference: 0.5%; 95% CI: −28.7, +21.6). A higher risk was seen in the subset with undetectable HBsAb at 4 years, with rates of 15.5% for dual therapy and 36.8% for triple therapy (difference: −21.3%; 95% CI: −30.3, −13.8).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that switching to a TFV-sparing dual therapy was not associated with an increased risk of virological failure compared with continuing a triple regimen in this population.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that TFV-sparing dual therapy may be a viable option for virologically suppressed people living with HIV and past HBV infection, particularly for those with detectable HBsAb.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence strength is moderate due to the observational emulation of a target trial, which may be subject to residual confounding despite weighted analysis.

analysis.summary_en: This study emulated a target trial to compare tenofovir-based triple regimens with tenofovir-sparing dual therapies in 415 virologically suppressed adults living with HIV and past HBV infection. Using a weighted Kaplan–Meier estimator, the analysis found no significant difference in the 5-year risk of virological failure between the two strategies (29.3% vs. 29.9%). However, a higher risk of failure was observed in the subset of participants with undetectable HBsAb at 4 years, regardless of treatment group. The authors conclude that switching to a dual therapy is not associated with increased virological failure risk, suggesting it may be a safe alternative for this patient population.

title: Correlates of hepatitis B virus awareness and disease specific knowledge in Uganda: a meta-analysis and meta-regression of studies published between 2018 and 2025

analysis.research_question_and_background: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) remains a major public health challenge in Uganda, where prevalence varies by region and population group despite national vaccination and screening initiatives. This study synthesized available evidence on the correlates of HBV awareness and disease specific knowledge among different Ugandan populations.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This meta-analysis and meta-regression included eighteen cross-sectional studies reporting on HBV awareness or disease-specific knowledge in Uganda, published between January 2018 and December 2025. The studies encompassed various population groups, including the general population, healthcare workers, and antenatal care attendees.
analysis.methods: Two reviewers independently conducted study selection, data extraction, and quality appraisal using the Joanna Briggs Institute Critical Appraisal Checklist. Pooled estimates of HBV awareness and correlates of disease-specific knowledge were computed using a random-effects model in MedCalc software, with heterogeneity quantified using the I2 statistic, and meta-regression was performed to examine trends by region, year, and study population.
analysis.main_results: The pooled prevalence of HBV awareness was 75.3% (95% CI: 61.5%-86.9%) with substantial heterogeneity (I2=99.24%). Awareness was significantly higher in Central Uganda compared to other regions and among healthcare workers compared to the general population and antenatal care attendees (p < 0.05). Meta-regression revealed a paradoxical overall decline in HBV awareness over the study period.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Critical gaps persist in HBV awareness and key knowledge areas, such as post-exposure prophylaxis and full vaccination schedule completion, despite moderate awareness of transmission routes. The authors interpret the findings as highlighting the need for alternative strategies tailored to the social dynamics of the current generation during the delivery of health messages.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Understanding awareness and knowledge levels is essential for guiding HBV prevention and control strategies. The findings suggest that targeted health education interventions are necessary to address specific knowledge deficits and improve vaccination uptake among different Ugandan populations.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence strength is moderate due to the substantial heterogeneity observed across regions and population groups. The study design relied on cross-sectional data, which limits causal inference, and the paradoxical decline in awareness over time warrants further investigation.

analysis.summary_en: This meta-analysis synthesized evidence from eighteen cross-sectional studies to evaluate Hepatitis B virus (HBV) awareness and knowledge correlates in Uganda between 2018 and 2025. The pooled prevalence of HBV awareness was 75.3%, with substantial heterogeneity across regions and populations. Awareness was significantly higher in Central Uganda and among healthcare workers compared to the general population and antenatal care attendees. While knowledge of transmission routes was moderate, critical gaps remained regarding post-exposure prophylaxis and vaccination schedules. Meta-regression indicated a paradoxical overall decline in awareness over the study period. These findings highlight the need for tailored health education strategies to address persistent knowledge deficits and guide effective HBV prevention and control efforts.

title: Enhanced surveillance for hepatitis B and C: insights into clinical care after diagnosis

analysis.research_question_and_background: There are known gaps in care uptake for hepatitis B virus (HBV) and hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection, and public health surveillance represents an opportunity to support health service engagement for cases; however, specific data are lacking regarding follow-up after diagnosis.
analysis.study_design_and_population: Notified cases of HBV and HCV within Victoria during 2023-2024 were analysed to determine post-diagnosis follow-up, including variation by demographics and setting.
analysis.methods: The study assessed outcomes of a Victorian initiative to enhance data availability and to support linkage to care by analysing notified cases and reported reasons for lack of linkage to care.
analysis.main_results: Information was available for two-thirds of cases. For HBV, 37.7% reported current treatment or management, while 53.6% reported referral or assessment in progress; for HCV, these proportions were 33.3% and 54.7%.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Cascade of care information can be effectively collected via public health surveillance, and these systems represent an opportunity to support prioritisation of public health follow-up.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that enhanced surveillance systems can be utilised to support the prioritisation of public health follow-up and improve linkage to care for viral hepatitis cases.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The supplied evidence does not report specific design limitations, bias, confounding, or a detailed assessment of evidence strength.

analysis.summary_en: This study assessed a Victorian initiative from 2023 to 2024 aimed at enhancing data availability and supporting linkage to care for notified hepatitis B virus (HBV) and hepatitis C virus (HCV) cases. Analysis of post-diagnosis follow-up revealed that information was available for two-thirds of cases. For HBV, 37.7% reported current treatment or management and 53.6% reported referral or assessment in progress, while for HCV, these proportions were 33.3% and 54.7% respectively. Reasons for gaps in care included loss to follow-up, cost barriers, and misapplication of HBV treatment criteria. The authors conclude that cascade of care information can be effectively collected via public health surveillance, offering an opportunity to support the prioritisation of public health follow-up.

title: Hepatitis B virus infection with high HBsAg and undetectable DNA levels in untreated blood donors: Viral mechanisms and transfusion safety implications

analysis.research_question_and_background: Blood donor screening occasionally identifies individuals with high HBV surface antigen (HBsAg) levels despite undetectable or extremely low HBV DNA, but the molecular basis and transfusion risk of this discordant profile remain unclear.
analysis.study_design_and_population: Seventy-five blood donors with HBsAg >100 IU/mL and undetectable or very low HBV DNA (<6 IU/mL), including 39 ID-NAT-nonreactive, were investigated.
analysis.methods: HBV DNA was further assessed using a second ID-NAT assay, confirmatory PCR following virion concentration, and sequencing; selected basic core promoter (BCP) and core mutations were introduced into replication-competent HBV plasmids to assess effects on extracellular virion-associated DNA production.
analysis.main_results: Four (5%) samples were nonreactive by the two ID-NAT assays; HBV DNA was confirmed in all donors, often at unquantifiable levels, and all were anti-HBc positive; no consistent molecular signature was identified, but heterogeneous, case-specific mutations were detected in BCP, core, and PreS1.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The HBsAg-positive/low-DNA profile largely reflects chronic inactive infection with minimal viremia, and diverse regulatory and structural mutations may contribute in a multifactorial manner.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Persistent viral genomes and residual replication support continued HBsAg screening where NAT sensitivity is suboptimal and anti-HBc testing cannot be implemented.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence strength is moderate, as the study identified no consistent molecular signature and relied on in vitro assays to confirm mutation effects, though the sample size was adequate for the observed findings.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated 75 blood donors with high HBsAg (>100 IU/mL) and undetectable or very low HBV DNA (<6 IU/mL), including 39 ID-NAT-nonreactive cases. HBV DNA was confirmed in all donors, often at unquantifiable levels, with all testing anti-HBc positive. No consistent molecular signature was identified, but heterogeneous mutations in BCP, core, and PreS1 regions were detected. In vitro experiments showed that selected BCP mutations reduced extracellular HBV DNA without affecting HBsAg production, while some core mutations impaired virion secretion. The authors concluded that this discordant profile reflects chronic inactive infection with minimal viremia, driven by diverse regulatory and structural mutations. The findings support continued HBsAg screening in settings with suboptimal NAT sensitivity and limited anti-HBc testing.

title: Structural barriers drive the intention-action gap in hepatitis B prevention among migrants in Shandong Province, China: a triangulated study of serological, spatial, and behavioral data.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection remains a major public health challenge in China. Migrant workers constitute a highly vulnerable population due to high geographic mobility and occupational vulnerability.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A triangulated cross-sectional study was conducted in Yantai, China, involving structured questionnaire surveys (N = 1,184) and serological testing (N = 2,364).
analysis.methods: The spatial distribution of regional anti-HBs positive rates was mapped using Geographic Information Systems (GIS). An adapted Health Belief Model was tested using Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) with a Robust Maximum Likelihood estimator to evaluate the disruptive effects of objective structural constraints-specifically, time poverty, economic constraints, and systemic lack of medical insurance.
analysis.main_results: The serologically confirmed anti-HBs positive rate was 51.10% (1,208/2,364), substantially lower than the 70% threshold recommended by the World Health Organization. Spatial analysis revealed significant geographic heterogeneity (χ2 = 74.38, P < 0.001), with higher immunity concentrated in large-scale industrial belts (67.33%) and lower immunity clustered in dispersed service-sector districts (36.81%). SEM results indicated that while external cues strongly predicted HBV knowledge (β = 0.894), knowledge had only a marginal effect on preventive intention (β = 0.192). Preventive intention significantly predicted actual behavior (β = 0.655).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The intention-action gap in HBV prevention among migrant workers is primarily driven by socioeconomic structural barriers-most notably time poverty, while basic HBV knowledge remains a foundational but insufficient condition for preventive action.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Achieving the goal of viral hepatitis elimination requires a shift from individual cognitive persuasion to structural interventions, emphasizing workplace-based service delivery, spatially targeted resource allocation, and insurance reforms to alleviate out-of-pocket and opportunity costs.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's findings are limited by its cross-sectional design, which cannot establish causality, and by the potential for unmeasured confounding factors. The evidence is moderate in strength due to the reliance on self-reported data and the absence of longitudinal follow-up.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the intention-action gap in hepatitis B virus (HBV) prevention among migrant workers in Shandong Province, China, using a triangulated approach integrating serological, spatial, and behavioral data. It finds that HBV immunity rates are lower than WHO recommendations, with significant geographic variation. Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) reveals that while external cues strongly predict HBV knowledge, knowledge has only a marginal effect on preventive intention, which significantly predicts actual behavior. The study attributes the gap primarily to socioeconomic structural barriers, particularly time poverty, rather than cognitive deficits. The findings suggest that structural interventions, such as workplace-based service delivery and insurance reforms, are essential for HBV prevention. However, the cross-sectional design limits the ability to establish causality, and the evidence is moderate in strength due to reliance on self-reported data.

title: Impact of Switching from Tenofovir Disoproxil Fumarate to Tenofovir Alafenamide or Entecavir in Older Patients with Chronic Hepatitis B

analysis.research_question_and_background: Tenofovir disoproxil fumarate (TDF) is highly effective for chronic hepatitis B (CHB) but may induce progressive renal impairment and proximal tubular dysfunction; switching to tenofovir alafenamide (TAF) or entecavir (ETV) may reduce TDF-related nephrotoxicity.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This retrospective longitudinal cohort study included adults with CHB who switched from TDF to TAF or ETV at a tertiary center (2012-2023), with eligible patients having ≥ 2 years of TDF treatment and ≥ 2 years of post-switch follow-up.
analysis.methods: Clinical and laboratory data were collected at 6-month intervals from 2 years before to 4 years after switching; biomarker trajectories were analyzed using linear mixed-effects models with time centered at switch comparing treatments and with multivariable adjustment for key confounders.
analysis.main_results: A total of 102 patients were included (TAF n = 82; ETV n = 20), mean age 72 ± 10 years, 72% male; serum creatinine showed a non-significant increasing trend during TDF therapy (β = +0.008 mg/dL/year, p = 0.24) and after switching (β = +0.009 mg/dL/year, p = 0.07), with no significant difference between groups; serum phosphate declined during TDF in the ETV group (β = -0.175 mg/dL/year, p = 0.002) and showed a significant increase after switching (β = +0.111 mg/dL/year, p = 0.031) while the TAF group remained stable; total cholesterol showed a significant immediate increase at the time of switch (+18.3 mg/dL, 95% CI 11.0-25.6, p < 0.001), with no significant difference between TAF and ETV.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Unlike previous studies reporting clear creatinine improvement after switching from TDF, this cohort did not show a statistically significant reduction in creatinine levels after the switch although an attenuation of creatinine progression and recovery of phosphate levels were observed, suggesting mitigation of TDF-related renal and tubular toxicity.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform clinical practice by suggesting that switching from TDF to TAF or ETV in older patients may mitigate renal and tubular toxicity, though the absence of significant creatinine reduction warrants careful monitoring.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its retrospective design and small sample size, particularly for the ETV group (n = 20), which may reduce generalizability; however, the longitudinal analysis with multivariable adjustment provides moderate evidence strength.

analysis.summary_en: This retrospective cohort study evaluated renal and metabolic changes in 102 older patients with chronic hepatitis B who switched from tenofovir disoproxil fumarate (TDF) to tenofovir alafenamide (TAF) or entecavir (ETV). Despite previous studies suggesting creatinine improvement after switching, this cohort showed no significant reduction in creatinine levels, though an attenuation of progression and phosphate recovery were observed. Serum phosphate declined during TDF in the ETV group but increased after switching, while total cholesterol showed an immediate increase at the time of switch. The findings suggest mitigation of TDF-related renal and tubular toxicity, though the absence of significant creatinine reduction highlights the need for careful monitoring in older patients.

title: Factors Associated With Surface Antigen (HBsAg) Clearance in a Spanish Cohort of Chronic Hepatitis B Patients: Influence on the Long‐Term Prognosis

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to identify factors contributing to hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) clearance in patients with chronic hepatitis B (CHB) infection and assess its influence on long-term prognosis.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A prospective open cohort study of 453 patients with CHB infection was conducted in the Liver Unit of two hospitals in Málaga, Spain, between 1991 and 2022. The incidence of HBsAg clearance was 1.96 cases per 100 patient-years.
analysis.methods: A multivariate Cox regression analysis was used to identify factors associated with HBsAg clearance. The impact of clearance on long-term prognosis was evaluated using a combined prognostic endpoint: need for liver transplantation, liver complications, or liver-related mortality.
analysis.main_results: During follow-up, 96/453 patients (21.2%) lost HBsAg, with an incidence rate of 1.96/100 patients per year.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: HBsAg clearance was associated with a better long-term hepatic prognosis, highlighting its significance in disease outcomes.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform surveillance and management strategies for chronic hepatitis B patients, emphasizing the importance of HBsAg clearance in predicting favorable long-term outcomes.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its observational design and potential confounding factors, but the evidence is strong due to the large sample size and long follow-up period.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated factors associated with hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) clearance in a Spanish cohort of chronic hepatitis B patients and its impact on long-term prognosis. A prospective open cohort study of 453 patients with chronic hepatitis B infection was conducted between 1991 and 2022 in Málaga, Spain. The study used multivariate Cox regression analysis to identify independent factors linked to HBsAg clearance, including age over 40 years, baseline HBV DNA levels below 3.3 log 10, and loss of hepatitis B e-antigen during follow-up. The results showed that 21.2% of patients lost HBsAg, with an incidence rate of 1.96 cases per 100 patient-years. HBsAg clearance was associated with improved long-term hepatic prognosis, as measured by the combined endpoint of liver transplantation, complications, or mortality. The study's evidence is strong due to its large sample size and extended follow-up, though its observational design limits causal inference.

title: Chronic HBV Infection Disrupts CCL5‐Secreting cNK Cells and Attenuates Liver Accumulation and Activation of DCs and HBV‐Specific T Cells

analysis.research_question_and_background: Understanding the immunological mechanisms underlying chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection-induced immune tolerance is critical for developing effective therapeutic strategies, yet the mechanisms by which natural killer (NK)-cell subsets regulate dendritic cell (DC)-mediated antiviral immunity during chronic HBV infection remain unclear.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study demonstrated that chronic HBV infection disrupted intrahepatic DCs accumulation and activation by suppressing CC chemokine ligand 5 (CCL5) production from hepatic NK cells.
analysis.methods: The study involved the adoptive transfer of CCL5-competent hepatic conventional NK (cNK) cells to promote DCs accumulation and activation, enhancing HBV-specific CD8+ T-cell responses and facilitating viral clearance.
analysis.main_results: Chronic HBV infection reduced the number of hepatic cNK cells, the main source of hepatic CCL5, whereas liver-resident NK (LrNK) cells increased and exhibited lower CCL5 expression and immunosuppressive features.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Chronic HBV infection promoted the activation of adenosine A2a receptor (ADORA2A)/nuclear factor kappa-B (NF-κB) pathway in hepatic NK cells, thereby antagonizing NF-κB activation, reducing the proportion of cNK cells, suppressing CCL5 production, and ultimately impairing hepatic aggregation and activation of DCs, leading to defective anti-HBV immune responses.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: This study revealed a novel mechanism involved in chronic HBV infection-induced immune tolerance and indicated that targeting the ADORA2A/NFκB/CCL5 axis in cNK cells may represent a potential therapeutic strategy for chronic HBV infection.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study provides strong evidence for the role of cNK cells in regulating DC-mediated antiviral immunity during chronic HBV infection, but further research is needed to validate these findings in clinical settings.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the immunological mechanisms underlying chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection-induced immune tolerance, focusing on the role of natural killer (NK) cell subsets in regulating dendritic cell (DC)-mediated antiviral immunity. The research demonstrates that chronic HBV infection disrupts intrahepatic DCs accumulation and activation by suppressing CC chemokine ligand 5 (CCL5) production from hepatic NK cells. Specifically, chronic HBV infection reduces the number of hepatic conventional NK (cNK) cells, which are the main source of hepatic CCL5, while liver-resident NK (LrNK) cells increase and exhibit lower CCL5 expression and immunosuppressive features. Adoptive transfer of CCL5-competent hepatic cNK cells promotes DCs accumulation and activation, enhances HBV-specific CD8+ T-cell responses, and facilitates viral clearance. Mechanistically, chronic HBV infection activates the adenosine A2a receptor (ADORA2A)/nuclear factor kappa-B (NF-κB) pathway in hepatic NK cells, antagonizing NF-κB activation, reducing the proportion of cNK cells, suppressing CCL5 production, and impairing hepatic aggregation and activation of DCs. This study reveals a novel mechanism involved in chronic HBV infection-induced immune tolerance and suggests that targeting the ADORA2A/NFκB/CCL5 axis in cNK cells may represent a potential therapeutic strategy for chronic HBV infection. The findings provide strong evidence for the role of cNK cells in regulating DC-mediated antiviral immunity during chronic HBV infection, but further research is needed to validate these findings in clinical settings.

title: Medication adherence in Chinese adults with chronic hepatitis B based on theory of planned behavior

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate factors related to medication adherence in patients with chronic hepatitis B (CHB) infection using the theory of planned behavior (TPB).
analysis.study_design_and_population: This cross-sectional study included 225 patients with CHB recruited from the outpatient department of Qingdao Public Health Clinical Center in China.
analysis.methods: Pearson correlation analysis was used to evaluate associations between medication adherence and TPB items, and a structural equation model was established to assess the effects of latent TPB variables on medication adherence.
analysis.main_results: Among 225 patients with CHB, 67.6% reported moderate medication adherence as assessed by the Morisky Adherence Assessment Score. Medication adherence was significantly positively correlated with behavioral intention (r = 0.51, P < 0.001), perceived behavioral control (r = 0.63, P < 0.001), and subjective norms (r = 0.52, P < 0.001).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that behavioral attitude, subjective norms, and perceived behavioral control indirectly affected medication adherence, with the structural equation model explaining 58.5% of the variance in medication adherence.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform interventions to improve medication adherence in CHB patients by targeting behavioral attitude, subjective norms, and perceived behavioral control based on the TPB framework.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was cross-sectional, limiting causal inference, but the large sample size and use of validated measures provide moderate evidence strength.

analysis.summary_en: This cross-sectional study investigated medication adherence in 225 Chinese adults with chronic hepatitis B using the theory of planned behavior (TPB). Results showed 67.6% of patients had moderate adherence, with significant positive correlations between adherence and behavioral intention (r = 0.51), perceived behavioral control (r = 0.63), and subjective norms (r = 0.52). The structural equation model revealed behavioral attitude and subjective norms as the strongest predictors, indirectly affecting adherence through behavioral intention, explaining 58.5% of variance. The findings suggest targeting these TPB components could improve adherence in CHB patients.

title: Trends in Hepatitis B, Hepatitis C, and HIV Seroprevalence in the Netherlands: Insights From Two Decades of Nationwide PIENTER Serosurveys.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Hepatitis B (HBV), hepatitis C (HCV), and HIV remain public health challenges despite effective treatments and preventive options, with infections often asymptomatic leading to undiagnosed cases and onward transmission. In the Netherlands, the disease burden is concentrated in specific populations with many undetected infections, necessitating an assessment of seroprevalence trends over time.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study utilized data from three nationwide cross-sectional serosurveys (PIENTER: 1995-1996, 2006-2007, and 2016-2017) including 14,444 participants aged 15-79 years to estimate HBV, HCV, and HIV seroprevalence, identify determinants, and assess trends over 20 years.
analysis.methods: Participants completed questionnaires on demographics, behaviour, and socio-economic factors, and serum samples were tested for HBV and HCV in all rounds and HIV in 2017. Seroprevalence estimates were weighted to the Dutch population, trends were analysed using weighted Poisson regression, and determinants were evaluated using multivariable Poisson regression.
analysis.main_results: Weighted HBV seroprevalence remained stable across surveys (3%-5% past or present infection; < 0.4% active infection), was highest among first-generation migrants, and only 9% of active HBV cases were aware of their status. HCV seroprevalence remained low (< 0.4%) and was highest among non-Western migrants, while HIV prevalence was 0.1% and highest among non-Western migrants and men who have sex with men.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Overall, HBV, HCV, and HIV seroprevalence remain low in the Netherlands but are concentrated in specific groups with limited awareness, indicating that while general population prevalence is stable, persistent transmission risks exist within these subpopulations.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings support targeted prevention, screening, and linkage-to-care strategies to achieve the 2030 WHO elimination goals and highlight the importance of continued population-based (sero-)monitoring to guide public health policy.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The supplied evidence does not report specific design limitations, bias, or confounding factors, but the use of weighted data from three large-scale nationwide surveys over two decades provides a moderate level of evidence for assessing population trends.

analysis.summary_en: This study analyzed three nationwide cross-sectional serosurveys (PIENTER) from 1995-1996, 2006-2007, and 2016-2017, involving 14,444 participants aged 15-79 years, to assess trends in HBV, HCV, and HIV seroprevalence in the Netherlands. Weighted analyses showed that HBV seroprevalence remained stable (3%-5% past or present infection; < 0.4% active infection), HCV stayed low (< 0.4%), and HIV prevalence was 0.1%. Infections were concentrated among first-generation and non-Western migrants and men who have sex with men, with only 9% of active HBV cases aware of their status. These findings support targeted prevention and screening strategies to achieve WHO elimination goals and underscore the need for continued population-based monitoring.

title: Spatiotemporal evolution characteristics and influencing factors of hepatitis B incidence rate in China

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to examine regional disparities in hepatitis B incidence, explore its spatiotemporal evolution patterns, and analyze the spatiotemporal heterogeneity of associated factors across China, using incidence data from 2008 to 2023.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study used incidence data from 2008 to 2023 across China to examine regional disparities, spatiotemporal evolution patterns, and the heterogeneity of influencing factors.
analysis.methods: The Dagum Gini coefficient decomposition method assessed regional disparity sources, the standard deviation ellipse explored spatiotemporal direction and global characteristics, exploratory spatial data analysis (ESDA) examined spatial correlation and aggregation, and the geographically and temporally weighted regression (GTWR) model was used to examine spatiotemporal heterogeneity of influencing factors.
analysis.main_results: Results showed narrowing regional disparities, declining spatial aggregation, and a standard deviation ellipse located in eastern and central regions with a southeastward shift, alongside the incidence gravity center moving 351.25 km southeast.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Patterns shifted from clustered to dispersed, likely due to vaccination and improved healthcare allocation.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings provide insights into the spatiotemporal dynamics of hepatitis B incidence in China, which can inform targeted public health interventions and resource allocation.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The supplied evidence does not report specific limitations of the study.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the spatiotemporal evolution of hepatitis B incidence in China from 2008 to 2023, focusing on regional disparities and the heterogeneity of influencing factors. Using advanced spatial analysis techniques, the research reveals a trend of narrowing regional disparities and a shift in the spatial distribution of incidence towards the southeast. The findings suggest that public health interventions such as vaccination and improved healthcare allocation have contributed to these changes. The study highlights the importance of understanding the geographic and temporal patterns of hepatitis B to guide targeted prevention and control strategies. While the study provides valuable insights, it does not explicitly report limitations, which may affect the confidence in its conclusions.

title: Long-Term Outcomes of Entecavir Therapy in Treatment-Naive Patients with Chronic Hepatitis B

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study was needed to evaluate the long-term efficacy and safety of entecavir therapy and investigate predictors of partial virological response in treatment-naive chronic hepatitis B patients, addressing the need for effective long-term antiviral therapy to prevent disease progression.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This retrospective study included 230 nucleoside-naive chronic hepatitis B patients treated with entecavir between January 2020 and December 2024.
analysis.methods: Virological response was defined as HBV-DNA reduction of at least 1 log10 IU/mL with detectable viral DNA after at least 12 months of therapy, and clinical, biochemical, and virological parameters were analyzed during follow-up.
analysis.main_results: Virological response rates reached 66% at month 3, 86% at month 6, 89% at year 1, and 100% by years 4–5; partial virological response occurred in 10.2% of patients and was significantly associated with higher baseline HBV-DNA levels and failure to achieve virological response at week 24.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that entecavir therapy provides effective, durable viral suppression and excellent safety in treatment-naive chronic hepatitis B patients, and continued treatment in patients with partial virological response may still achieve complete virological suppression.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings support the use of entecavir as a first-line therapy for chronic hepatitis B, with implications for long-term viral suppression and reduced disease progression, and suggest that even patients with partial virological response may benefit from continued treatment.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence strength is moderate due to the retrospective study design and single-center population, which may limit generalizability, though the large sample size and long follow-up period provide robust data on entecavir's efficacy and safety.

analysis.summary_en: This retrospective study evaluated the long-term efficacy and safety of entecavir in 230 treatment-naive chronic hepatitis B patients over 5 years. Results showed virological response rates increasing from 66% at month 3 to 100% by years 4–5, with partial virological response in 10.2% of patients. Partial response was associated with higher baseline HBV-DNA and failure to achieve virological response at week 24. No serious adverse events were observed. The study demonstrates entecavir's effective viral suppression and safety profile, suggesting continued treatment may benefit even partial responders.

title: Longitudinal Patterns of Chronic Hepatitis B Care and Treatment Adherence in Australia: A National Linked Data Cohort Study.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Current uptake of chronic hepatitis B (CHB) treatment and care in Australia is well below target levels, leading to an ongoing burden of preventable liver disease and cancer.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This study analysed records of hepatitis B viral load (VL) testing and antiviral treatment provided through Australia's national health insurance system, which were linked to migration, death, and sociodemographic data from various government datasets.
analysis.methods: Treatment and VL testing by population group were assessed, and uptake was calculated using modelled estimates of the number living with CHB.
analysis.main_results: Of the estimated 219,800 people living with CHB in Australia in 2023, 118,334 (53.8%) received either VL testing or treatment during 2014-2023. Of the 81,360 who received any VL testing, only 17,352 (21.3%) received it regularly, while 31,715 (39.0%) had evidence of prior monitoring but no VL testing since 2019.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: This study shows that substantial gaps exist in CHB care in Australia, particularly in continued monitoring among those not on treatment.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Estimated uptake of VL testing and treatment uptake were lower among Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people and also varied by region of birth.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The supplied evidence does not report limitations of the study design.

analysis.summary_en: This study examines the patterns of chronic hepatitis B (CHB) care and treatment adherence in Australia using national health insurance and government datasets. It highlights that current treatment and care uptake is below target levels, contributing to preventable liver disease and cancer. The analysis reveals disparities in VL testing and treatment among Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander populations and by region of birth. While the majority of those who initiated treatment continued therapy, significant gaps in monitoring persist for those not on treatment. analysis.research_question_and_background: Liver disease linked to the hepatitis B virus (HBV) is a serious public threat worldwide and in Egypt, with an infection incidence of about 1.4%. analysis.main_results: Significant differences were found in hemoglobin, albumin, and INR levels between the groups, with median FIB-4 scores of 1.26 vs 0.79 and median APRI scores of 0.40 vs 0.27 in the significant fibrosis group. The FIB-4 index remained a significant predictor of significant fibrosis in multivariate analysis with an odds ratio of 1.558, and at a cut-off value of >0.88, it achieved a sensitivity of 65.42% and a specificity of 60.0%.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Although the use of FIB-4 score is potentially useful in resource-limited settings, a significant number of misclassifications can occur due to its moderate sensitivity and specificity. This necessitates the further incorporation of additional diagnostic methods to ensure the accurate staging of liver fibrosis.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Accurate liver fibrosis assessments are crucial in the evaluation and follow-up of HBV patients, but traditional biopsies have limitations, prompting the use of non-invasive methods like VCTE. The findings suggest that while FIB-4 offers a more accessible and less costly approach, its moderate diagnostic performance requires supplementation with other methods for reliable disease management.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The supplied evidence does not report specific design limitations or biases beyond the moderate sensitivity and specificity of the FIB-4 score. The evidence strength is moderate due to the cross-sectional design and the reliance on VCTE as the reference standard without biopsy confirmation.

analysis.summary_en: This cross-sectional study evaluated the diagnostic accuracy of FIB-4 and APRI scores against vibration controlled transient elastography (VCTE) in 247 Egyptian patients with chronic hepatitis B. VCTE classified 140 patients with no or mild fibrosis and 107 with significant fibrosis. Results showed that while FIB-4 and APRI scores were significantly higher in the significant fibrosis group, FIB-4 demonstrated only moderate diagnostic performance. At a cut-off of >0.88, FIB-4 achieved a sensitivity of 65.42% and specificity of 60.0%, remaining a significant predictor in multivariate analysis with an odds ratio of 1.558. title: High Prevalence of Occult Hepatitis B Virus Co-Infection Identified in Treponema Pallidum-Positive Blood Donations: Implications for HBV Risk Reduction

title: Optimizing Hepatitis B screening: A comparison of ELISA and rapid tests

The rapid diagnostic test had a sensitivity of 71.41% and a specificity of 100%, while the ELISA confirmed its superiority with sensitivities exceeding 95% and specificities close to 98%.

Optimizing hepatitis B screening in Madagascar relies on the complementary use of rapid tests for community-based screening and ELISA for diagnostic confirmation.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings underscore the urgency of early and targeted screening, combined with a strengthened vaccination strategy. title: Hepatitis B prevention practices and associated factors among medical and health sciences students at university of Gondar, Northwest Ethiopia

analysis.study_design_and_population: An institution-based mixed-methods cross-sectional study was conducted among 666 Medical and Health Sciences students at the University of Gondar from March to August 2025 using stratified sampling.
analysis.methods: Data were collected via a self-administered questionnaire and key informant interviews with instructors and students, analyzed using bi-variable and multivariable logistic regression and inductive thematic analysis.

analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest the University and Ministry of Health should provide practical training, address PPE shortages, ensure HBV screening and vaccination, and create culturally sensitive awareness campaigns.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The supplied evidence does not report specific design limitations or a detailed assessment of evidence strength beyond the cross-sectional nature of the study.

analysis.summary_en: This institution-based mixed-methods cross-sectional study assessed hepatitis B prevention practices among 666 Medical and Health Sciences students at the University of Gondar, Ethiopia, from March to August 2025. Multivariable analysis showed that being aged 20–24, being a Physiotherapy student, and having a favorable attitude were significantly associated with good prevention practices. Qualitative findings highlighted inadequate awareness, personal protective equipment shortages, and a reliance on traditional medicine. The authors recommend that the University and Ministry of Health provide practical training, address resource shortages, ensure vaccination, and develop culturally sensitive awareness campaigns to improve prevention practices.

title: Longitudinal Renal Function Changes and Pilot Mitochondrial Epigenetic Analysis in Chronic Hepatitis B Patients Treated with Nucleos(t)ide Analogues

analysis.research_question_and_background: Long-term use of nucleos(t)ide analogues has been associated with mitochondrial dysfunction and potential adverse effects. This study aimed to evaluate nephrotoxicity in treated and treatment-naïve chronic hepatitis B patients and to explore DNA methyltransferase 1 expression as a potential epigenetic mechanism.
analysis.study_design_and_population: Adult chronic hepatitis B patients receiving tenofovir disoproxil fumarate or entecavir for at least 12 months comprised the under-treatment group, while untreated patients formed the treatment-naïve group. A total of 158 patients were analyzed, including 91 treated and 67 treatment-naïve individuals.
analysis.methods: Renal parameters at baseline and months 3, 6, and 12 were analyzed retrospectively, and longitudinal changes in glomerular filtration rate were assessed using linear mixed-effects modeling. DNA methyltransferase 1 expression in peripheral blood mononuclear cells was evaluated as a pilot analysis.
analysis.main_results: Median glomerular filtration rate values declined significantly from 102.3 at baseline to 102.1 at the 12th month in the treated group. Longitudinal analysis showed each additional time point was associated with a mean GFR decline of 1.65 mL/min/1.73m2, and age was independently associated with a reduction in GFR. No significant differences in renal outcomes were observed between tenofovir disoproxil fumarate and entecavir, and DNA methyltransferase 1 expression was comparable between groups.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as indicating a significant decline in renal function over time in treated patients, with age identified as an independent factor. The study suggests that while nephrotoxicity is present, it does not differ significantly between the two specific nucleos(t)ide analogues studied.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings cautiously inform the monitoring of renal function in chronic hepatitis B patients undergoing long-term nucleos(t)ide analogue therapy. The results suggest that vigilance regarding kidney health is warranted regardless of the specific agent used.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence strength is moderate due to the retrospective design and the abstract-only nature of the available data. The pilot epigenetic analysis was limited to a small sample size of 25 patients.

analysis.summary_en: This retrospective study evaluated nephrotoxicity and DNA methyltransferase 1 expression in 158 chronic hepatitis B patients, comparing those treated with tenofovir disoproxil fumarate or entecavir for at least 12 months to treatment-naïve controls. Longitudinal analysis revealed a statistically significant decline in median glomerular filtration rate in the treated group over 12 months, with age identified as an independent factor for reduced renal function. No significant differences in renal outcomes were observed between the two nucleos(t)ide analogues, and the pilot epigenetic analysis found comparable DNA methyltransferase 1 expression between groups. These findings suggest the need for renal monitoring during long-term therapy, though the evidence is limited by the retrospective design and small pilot sample.

title: Effects of Silica Infused with Gold/Silver/Platinum on the Hepatitis B Drug Entecavir by Theoretical Investigation

analysis.research_question_and_background: Chronic hepatitis B virus infection remains a deadly global health issue affecting around 275 million individuals despite the availability of effective vaccines. This study investigated the adsorption behavior of the hepatitis B drug Entecavir on silica infused with gold, silver, and platinum nanocomposites to explore potential drug delivery improvements.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The supplied evidence does not report a specific study design, setting, dates, or human or animal population. The research utilized a theoretical computational approach involving density functional theory and molecular docking simulations to analyze the interaction between the drug Entecavir and metal-infused silica nanocomposites.
analysis.methods: The study employed density functional theory linked to the B3LYP functional with a combined basis set of 6-311++g(d,p) and LANL2DZ to optimize geometry and calculate adsorption energies. Natural Bond Orbital and Molecular Electrostatic Potential analyses were conducted to assess electron transfer and active sites, while molecular docking was performed to evaluate binding interactions with proteins 3OX8 and 3OXR.
analysis.main_results: Entecavir adsorbed on silver, gold, and platinum-infused silica via its NH2 group with counterpoise-corrected energies of -60.13, -39.39, and -48.33 kcal/mol, respectively. Molecular docking revealed that the drug-nanocomposite complexes effectively bind to proteins 3OX8 and 3OXR, with binding energies of -4.87, -6.11, -9.72, and -9.35 kcal/mol for Entecavir and the platinum complex, respectively, forming multiple hydrogen bonds.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the electron transfer from the nanocomposites to the drug and the favorable binding energies as confirmation of silica's role as an electron donor and the enhanced stability of the complexes. The novelty lies in the theoretical demonstration that metal-doped silica nanocomposites can create active sites for effective Entecavir adsorption and potentially improve its biological activity.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings suggest that silica infused with gold, silver, or platinum could serve as effective nanocarriers for the delivery of Entecavir. This theoretical insight may inform the future development of optimized drug delivery systems to enhance the treatment efficacy for chronic hepatitis B virus infection.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence strength is low because the study is entirely theoretical and computational, lacking in vitro or in vivo validation. The supplied evidence does not report experimental data, sample sizes, or physical synthesis of the nanocomposites, which limits the ability to confirm the biological relevance of the calculated interactions.

analysis.summary_en: This theoretical study investigated the adsorption of the hepatitis B drug Entecavir on silica infused with gold, silver, and platinum nanocomposites using density functional theory and molecular docking. Results showed that Entecavir adsorbed via its NH2 group with energies ranging from -60.13 to -39.39 kcal/mol and formed stable complexes with target proteins, exhibiting binding energies between -4.87 and -9.72 kcal/mol. The authors concluded that these metal-doped nanocomposites act as electron donors and enhance drug stability, suggesting their potential as effective nanocarriers for hepatitis B treatment. However, the evidence strength is low due to the absence of experimental validation.

title: Multiomics and artificial intelligence identify infection associated subtypes and prognostic signatures in hepatocellular carcinoma

analysis.research_question_and_background: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains a major global health burden with persistently high morbidity and mortality, and dysregulation of the tumor microenvironment associated with chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV)/hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection contributes to tumor progression and adverse outcomes. The study aimed to address the limitation that many existing HCC prognostic models do not systematically integrate infection-associated molecular signatures with immune and genomic features.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This study established an integrated predictive framework based on multi-cohort transcriptomic, somatic mutation, immune infiltration, and clinical data from public databases including TCGA-LIHC, ICGC-LIRI-JP, and GEO-GSE14520. The prognostic risk model was developed in the TCGA-LIHC training cohort and externally validated in ICGC-LIRI-JP and GSE14520 cohorts.
analysis.methods: The researchers constructed a comprehensive 248-gene infection-associated set covering HBV/HCV infection, antiviral responses, and immune regulation, and identified two robust HCC molecular subtypes through unsupervised consensus clustering. They screened 12 core prognostic genes using three complementary machine learning algorithms and evaluated the model using area under the curve (AUC) values, hazard ratios, and decision curve analysis.
analysis.main_results: The study identified two HCC molecular subtypes with distinct infection-status annotations, immune infiltration features, genomic alteration profiles, and clinical prognosis. The prognostic risk model achieved 1-year AUC values of 0.82, 0.78, and 0.75 in the TCGA-LIHC, ICGC-LIRI-JP, and GSE14520 cohorts, respectively, and showed independent prognostic value for HCC with a hazard ratio of 2.87 (P < 0.001).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The results suggest associations among infection-associated molecular characteristics, tumor microenvironment remodeling, and HCC prognosis. The authors interpret the findings as indicating that the infection-associated signature may support retrospective HCC risk stratification.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The infection-associated signature may support retrospective HCC risk stratification, offering potential improvements in predictive performance for infection-associated HCC populations compared to traditional clinicopathological models. Prospective validation is required before routine clinical application.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence strength is moderate due to the reliance on retrospective cohorts and the need for future prospective studies.

analysis.summary_en: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is a major global health burden often associated with chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) or hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection. This study developed an integrated predictive framework using multi-cohort transcriptomic, genomic, and clinical data to address gaps in existing prognostic models. The researchers constructed a 248-gene infection-associated set, identified two distinct HCC molecular subtypes, and developed a 12-gene prognostic risk model using machine learning. The model demonstrated robust performance in training and validation cohorts, with 1-year AUC values ranging from 0.75 to 0.82 and independent prognostic value (HR = 2.87, P < 0.001). These findings suggest that infection-associated molecular characteristics are linked to tumor microenvironment remodeling and HCC prognosis. While the signature shows promise for retrospective risk stratification, prospective validation is necessary before clinical application.

title: Seroprevalence Trends of HBV, HCV, and HIV Before and During the COVID-19 Pandemic: Five-Year Retrospective Data from a Tertiary Hospital in Northern Cyprus

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to assess five-year seroreactivity trends of hepatitis B virus (HBV), hepatitis C virus (HCV), and human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) in Northern Cyprus, with emphasis on the coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) and post-pandemic periods.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This retrospective cross-sectional study evaluated 278,016 serological test results from a tertiary hospital in Northern Cyprus between 2020 and 2024.
analysis.methods: Tests for hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg), anti-HCV, and anti-HIV were performed using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay technology on the ARCHITECT Plus ci4100 system, with annual rates of seroreactivity calculated and compared across years and sex groups.
analysis.main_results: Overall seroreactivity rates were 1.2% for HBsAg, 0.6% for anti-HCV, and 0.2% for anti-HIV; HBV seroreactivity declined significantly from 1.5% in 2020 to 1.0% in 2023-2024 (p=0.001), while HCV prevalence increased non-significantly from 0.5% to 0.7% (p=0.192) and HIV prevalence remained stable at 0.2% (p=0.043).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as indicating that Northern Cyprus remains a low-endemic region, noting a declining trend in HBV seroreactivity, a rising trend in HCV levels, and stable low levels of HIV.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings highlight the importance of sustained surveillance and prevention efforts for these blood-borne infections in the post-COVID-19 era.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The authors stated that results need to be interpreted cautiously as they may not entirely indicate the levels of infection, and the evidence is assessed as moderate due to the retrospective design and reliance on serological data from a single center.

analysis.summary_en: This retrospective cross-sectional study evaluated 278,016 serological test results for HBV, HCV, and HIV in Northern Cyprus between 2020 and 2024. Overall seroreactivity rates were 1.2% for HBsAg, 0.6% for anti-HCV, and 0.2% for anti-HIV. HBV seroreactivity declined significantly from 1.5% in 2020 to 1.0% in 2023-2024 (p=0.001), while HCV prevalence showed a non-significant increase from 0.5% to 0.7% and HIV prevalence remained stable at 0.2%. The authors conclude that Northern Cyprus remains a low-endemic region and emphasize the importance of sustained surveillance and prevention in the post-COVID-19 era, though they note that results should be interpreted cautiously as they may not fully reflect infection levels.

title: Supramolecular Self-Assembly of Lycorine with Glycyrrhizic Acid into a Nanodrug for Safe and Sustained Anti-HBV Therapy

analysis.research_question_and_background: Achieving a functional cure for chronic hepatitis B remains a major challenge, as conventional therapies struggle to eliminate the hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) and subsequently restore adaptive antiviral immunity.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study designed a self-assembled nanomedicine (LGN) by co-assembling lycorine with glycyrrhizic acid to overcome the limitations of lycorine and enhance its therapeutic potential against HBV.
analysis.methods: The strategy involved co-assembling lycorine with glycyrrhizic acid to create a nanomedicine that protected lycorine from premature degradation, enabled sustained release in the colon, and attenuated systemic toxicity.
analysis.main_results: LGN effectively suppressed HBsAg secretion (IC 50 = 2.15 ± 0.09 μM) with a selectivity index (SI > 93) over two-fold higher than that of lycorine alone (SI = 39.26), and concurrently inhibited HBV DNA replication, pgRNA transcription, and the expression of viral proteins HBc and HBx.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that LGN induces a distinct host transcriptional program that disrupts multiple critical stages of the HBV life cycle, including viral entry, covalently closed circular DNA maintenance, gene transcription, and immune evasion, representing a multitargeted, host-dependent mechanism distinct from nucleos(t)ide analogs.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings provide valuable insights into exploiting natural products like lycorine for antiviral therapy and underscore the potential of self-assembly technology in improving drug safety and pharmacokinetic profiles for HBV treatment.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study demonstrates therapeutic potential against HBV with apparent safety in the HDI model, but the evidence strength is moderate as it is based on an abstract-only report without detailed methods or long-term clinical data.

analysis.summary_en: This study addresses the challenge of achieving a functional cure for chronic hepatitis B by developing a self-assembled nanomedicine (LGN) using lycorine and glycyrrhizic acid. LGN overcomes the limitations of lycorine, such as cytotoxicity and short half-life, by enabling sustained release and reducing systemic toxicity. The nanomedicine effectively suppresses HBsAg secretion with a higher selectivity index than lycorine alone and inhibits multiple stages of the HBV life cycle, including DNA replication and viral protein expression. Transcriptomic analysis reveals LGN disrupts critical HBV lifecycle stages through a host-dependent mechanism. This approach highlights the potential of natural products and self-assembly technology for safer and more effective HBV therapy.

title: Willingness to accept the HBV vaccine and related factors: Administering the vaccination attitudes examination scale to Urban Vietnamese adults

analysis.research_question_and_background: Vietnam has low hepatitis B vaccination coverage among adults, posing a threat to the healthcare system. To mitigate negative impacts, it is essential to identify vaccine hesitancy and refusal levels and their sociodemographic correlates.
analysis.study_design_and_population: We conducted a cross-sectional survey of 926 adults in Ho Chi Minh City (January–March 2025) using a self-administered questionnaire and the Vaccination Attitudes Examination (VAX) scale.
analysis.methods: Descriptive analysis was performed, and associations between variables were explored using a chi-square test. Multinomial logistic regression identified correlates of vaccine hesitancy and refusal, statistical significance was set at p < 0.05.
analysis.main_results: When analyzing general vaccine intentions regardless of vaccination status, 65.6% of participants indicated acceptance, 19.3% hesitancy, and 15.1% refusal. Vaccine refusal was primarily associated with a preference for natural immunity, while mistrust of vaccine benefits and commercial concerns were specifically linked to increased hesitancy.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: A unique 'knowledge paradox' was identified: poor knowledge about the HBV vaccine predicted outright refusal, whereas higher factual knowledge was positively correlated with mistrust of vaccine benefits, worries about future effects, and total VAX scores. This suggests that limited knowledge contribute to refusal, while greater factual knowledge coexisting with 'informed skepticism' or cautious hesitancy.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The VAX scale serves as a reliable instrument for assessing vaccine attitudes among urban Vietnamese adults. It helps identify key vaccine-related concerns and supports continuous monitoring of public attitudes, which is essential for designing effective vaccination programs and enhancing public trust in vaccines.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The supplied evidence does not report specific limitations or bias. The overall Cronbach's alpha was 0.833 (range = 0.812–0.919), and the McDonald's omega coefficients ranged from 0.820 to 0.920, indicating high evidence strength.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated hepatitis B vaccine acceptance among urban Vietnamese adults, finding that 65.6% accepted the vaccine, 19.3% were hesitant, and 15.1% refused. A 'knowledge paradox' emerged: poor knowledge predicted refusal, while higher knowledge correlated with mistrust and hesitancy. Vaccine refusal was linked to preference for natural immunity, while hesitancy stemmed from mistrust of benefits and commercial concerns. The VAX scale proved reliable for assessing attitudes, with high internal consistency (Cronbach's alpha = 0.833). These findings highlight the need for targeted interventions to address specific barriers and enhance vaccine acceptance.

title: Polygenic risk score and risk of drug-induced liver injury after initiating antiretroviral therapy in people living with HIV.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Drug-induced liver injury affects some people living with HIV (PWH) during antiretroviral therapy (ART). We examined associations of polygenic risk scores (PRS) with liver injury during ART.
analysis.study_design_and_population: We constructed PRS for individuals of African (AFR) and European (EUR) ancestry in 3,619 treatment-naïve participants from ART-naive studies of the Advancing Clinical Therapeutics Globally (ACTG) network.
analysis.methods: We derived PRS using summary statistics from the Veterans Affairs Million Veteran Program (MVP) and the Penn Medicine BioBank (PMBB). Liver injury was defined as incident grade 3 or greater alanine aminotransferase (ALT) within 48 weeks. Associations were evaluated by multivariable regression models.
analysis.main_results: Clinical variables associated with higher baseline ALT values included hepatitis B or C virus infection, increasing BMI and age, and male sex. In analyses of liver injury among 1,897 EUR participants (28 cases, 1869 controls) and 1722 AFR participants (21 cases, 1701 controls), HBV was associated with liver injury in both EUR and AFR participants, and HCV in EUR participants (p < 0.001 for each). PRSALT was not independently associated with incident liver injury in either EUR or AFR participants.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: No association was observed between baseline PRSALT and subsequent liver injury following initiation of ART.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that genetic risk scores for ALT may not predict drug-induced liver injury in PWH starting ART, highlighting the importance of clinical factors like HBV and HCV infection in monitoring liver health.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was limited by the small number of liver injury cases, particularly in the AFR group, which may reduce statistical power. The evidence strength is moderate due to the observational design and limited sample size for the outcome.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated whether polygenic risk scores (PRS) for alanine aminotransferase (ALT) could predict drug-induced liver injury in people living with HIV (PWH) initiating antiretroviral therapy (ART). Using data from 3,619 treatment-naïve participants of African and European ancestry, the researchers derived PRS and defined liver injury as grade 3 or greater ALT within 48 weeks. Clinical variables associated with higher baseline ALT included hepatitis B or C virus infection, increasing BMI and age, and male sex. While HBV was associated with liver injury in both ancestry groups and HCV in European participants, PRSALT was not independently associated with liver injury. The findings suggest that genetic risk for ALT may not predict liver injury in PWH starting ART, emphasizing the role of clinical factors like HBV and HCV in monitoring liver health.

title: Spatial Total RNA Sequencing of Formalin-Fixed Paraffin-Embedded Tissue by spRandom-seq.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addresses the challenge of spatially resolving comprehensive transcriptional landscapes in complex clinical tissues like formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded (FFPE) specimens to understand molecular pathogenesis in infectious diseases and cancer.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The research presents spRandom-seq, a spatial total RNA sequencing technology applied to FFPE tissues from mouse brain, olfactory bulb, breast cancer, Klebsiella pneumoniae-infected tissues, and hepatitis B virus (HBV)-positive hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC).
analysis.methods: spRandom-seq uses a random primer-based design to spatially resolve complete transcriptomes from host, bacteria, and nanoscale viruses in FFPE tissues, enabling discovery of lncRNAs, alternative splicing events, and spatial heterogeneity analysis.
analysis.main_results: In HBV-positive HCC samples, integrated analysis of host and viral RNAs revealed specific activation of complement and coagulation pathways across HBV-infected tumor areas, with an increased burden of copy number variations (CNVs).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret spRandom-seq as a practical and scalable approach for clinical pathology and infection diagnostics, leveraging its compatibility with existing platforms and minimal operational complexity.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings enable detailed spatial transcriptomic analysis of HBV infection in HCC, informing understanding of viral pathogenesis and potential diagnostic applications in clinical settings.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is derived solely from the abstract, limiting assessment of methodological rigor and validation; however, the technology's demonstrated applicability to multiple tissue types suggests moderate evidence strength.

analysis.summary_en: This study introduces spRandom-seq, a spatial total RNA sequencing technology designed to resolve comprehensive transcriptomes from host, microbial, and viral RNAs in FFPE tissues. Applied to HBV-positive HCC samples, the method revealed spatial activation of complement and coagulation pathways in HBV-infected tumor regions with increased CNVs. The technology's compatibility with existing platforms and minimal complexity make it a practical tool for clinical pathology and infection diagnostics, offering new insights into viral pathogenesis and spatial heterogeneity in cancer and infectious diseases.

title: Tumorigenesis of Hepatocellular Carcinoma Related to Metabolic Disorders With a Focus on the Hippo Pathway.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to determine the expression of Hippo pathway-related proteins in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and compare the data among patients with different underlying clinical background diseases, as the Hippo pathway has been implicated in HCC tumorigenesis.
analysis.study_design_and_population: We collected 40 resected HCC formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded samples and categorized them into 4 groups according to pre-existing conditions: 17 samples of alcohol consumption (HCC-A), 6 samples with hepatitis B virus infection (HCC-B), 8 samples with hepatitis C virus infection (HCC-C), and 9 samples with metabolic diseases (HCC-M).
analysis.methods: Using immunohistochemistry, we investigated the Hippo pathway-related proteins YAP1, CADM1, and SOX9 in the collected HCC samples.
analysis.main_results: Hypertension was the most common disease (72.5%) among patients with HCC, followed by diabetes mellitus (47.5%). Significant findings of steatohepatitis (SH) were observed in the HCC-A (35.3%) and HCC-M (88.9%) groups compared with those in the HCC-B (16.7%) and HCC-C (0%) groups. A significant finding of metabolic dysfunction-associated SH (MASH) was also observed in the HCC-M group (88.9%), and liver cirrhosis was predominantly observed in the HCC-C group (100%).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that Hippo pathway-associated proteins could serve as potential therapeutic targets for MASH and MASH-related HCC if the Hippo pathway is inactivated, as SH was more predominant in the HCC-M group with Hippo inactivity (100%) than in the HCC-A group (50.0%), and the average tumor size was significantly larger in the Hippo-inactive group than in the Hippo-active group.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that targeting the Hippo pathway could be a potential therapeutic strategy for MASH and MASH-related HCC, which may inform future treatment approaches and surveillance strategies for patients with metabolic disorders and HCC.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was limited by the small sample size (40 samples) and the retrospective nature of the data collection. The evidence strength is moderate due to the limited sample size and the lack of prospective validation.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the expression of Hippo pathway-related proteins in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and compared the data among patients with different underlying clinical background diseases. The researchers collected 40 resected HCC samples and categorized them into four groups based on pre-existing conditions: alcohol consumption (HCC-A), hepatitis B virus infection (HCC-B), hepatitis C virus infection (HCC-C), and metabolic diseases (HCC-M). Using immunohistochemistry, they analyzed the proteins YAP1, CADM1, and SOX9. The results showed that hypertension (72.5%) and diabetes mellitus (47.5%) were the most common diseases among HCC patients. Steatohepatitis (SH) was significantly more prevalent in the HCC-A (35.3%) and HCC-M (88.9%) groups compared to the HCC-B (16.7%) and HCC-C (0%) groups. Metabolic dysfunction-associated SH (MASH) was highly prevalent in the HCC-M group (88.9%), and liver cirrhosis was predominant in the HCC-C group (100%). The study concluded that Hippo pathway-associated proteins could serve as potential therapeutic targets for MASH and MASH-related HCC if the pathway is inactivated, as SH was more common in the HCC-M group with Hippo inactivity (100%) than in the HCC-A group (50.0%), and the average tumor size was significantly larger in the Hippo-inactive group. The findings suggest that targeting the Hippo pathway could be a promising therapeutic strategy for MASH and MASH-related HCC.

title: Incidence, risk factors and tumor spectrum of second primary cancers after gastric cancer: a multicenter cohort study with long-term follow-up.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addressed the poorly defined incidence, risk factors, and clinical implications of second primary cancers (SPCs) among gastric cancer (GC) survivors, aiming to quantify long-term risk and identify associated clinical factors.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This multicenter cohort study analyzed 11,027 GC survivors (8,519 men and 2,508 women) who underwent curative-intent radical gastrectomy between 2007 and 2021 within the Multidisciplinary Alliance of Gastric Integrative Studies (MAGIS) cohort.
analysis.methods: Clinical factors associated with SPC occurrence were identified using LASSO-penalized Cox regression, and an exploratory risk-based stratification model was developed. title: Droplet Digital PCR Measurement of HBV DNA in On-Treatment Chronic HBV Patients: Association With HCC Development and Outcomes.

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to investigate the association between low-level residual viremia in chronic hepatitis B patients on nucleos(t)ide analogues and the development of HBV-related hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC).
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study was a retrospective case-control analysis comparing 104 HCC patients with 104 non-HCC controls who were both on nucleos(t)ide analogues (NUCs) and had unquantifiable serum HBV DNA by the conventional Cobas-Taqman assay at HCC diagnosis.
analysis.methods: Residual viremia was measured using a validated high-sensitivity droplet digital polymerase chain reaction assay, which had a lower limit of detection of 1.6 IU/mL. Serum samples were collected at the time of HCC diagnosis, 1 year before, and 2 years before diagnosis.
analysis.main_results: Residual viremia within 2 years before HCC diagnosis was observed in 82.7% of HCC patients and 49.0% of controls (p < 0.001). It was independently associated with HCC occurrence (OR 7.243, 95% CI 1.862-28.170, p = 0.004).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that residual viremia is a significant factor in the development of HCC and its progression, highlighting the need for more sensitive monitoring methods.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings suggest that high-sensitivity HBV DNA assays could improve the monitoring of patients on NUCs, potentially leading to better management of HBV-related HCC risk.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its retrospective design and potential for confounding factors, but the evidence is strong due to the use of a validated high-sensitivity assay and clear statistical associations.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the association between residual viremia in chronic hepatitis B patients on nucleos(t)ide analogues (NUCs) and the development of HBV-related hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). It found that residual viremia within 2 years before HCC diagnosis was significantly more common in HCC patients compared to non-HCC controls, with an independent association with HCC occurrence. The study used a high-sensitivity droplet digital PCR assay to detect HBV DNA, revealing that residual viremia was also linked to more advanced tumor staging and poorer outcomes. These results suggest that improved monitoring with sensitive assays may be crucial for managing HCC risk in NUC-treated patients. However, the study's retrospective design and potential confounding factors limit the strength of the conclusions, though the evidence remains robust due to the clear statistical associations observed.

title: Monitoring of the Cascade of Care in Patients With Chronic HBV in Primary Care Clinics in Australia.

analysis.scope_and_question: This study focuses on hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection in primary care clinics in Australia, aiming to describe the prevalence of chronic HBV and the uptake of the cascade of care among patients.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: This prospective cohort study was conducted in 76 urban and regional primary care clinics across Victoria, Australia between 1/7/2020 and 30/6/2023, using anonymised socio-demographic, clinical and laboratory data from general practice electronic medical records.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The study found that only 13% of patients with HBV had evidence of at least one HBV DNA test and one ALT test ordered, 3% were reviewed by clinic staff, 17% by a viral hepatitis specialist, and 20% were on treatment, with significant gaps in the cascade of care.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The study highlights significant gaps in the cascade of care for people with chronic HBV in primary care settings, with a low proportion of patients participating in all stages of care, though specific controversies or unresolved mechanisms are not detailed.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The findings suggest a need for improved monitoring and management of HBV in primary care settings to address the gaps in the cascade of care and support Australia's goal of HBV elimination.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the cascade of care for chronic HBV in Australian primary care clinics, finding significant gaps in testing, specialist review, and treatment uptake. Among 491 patients with HBV, only 13% had evidence of both HBV DNA and ALT tests, 3% were reviewed by clinic staff, 17% by specialists, and 20% were on treatment. The results highlight the need for improved primary care management to achieve HBV elimination goals.
